candidates.architecture: records process-tree nondeterminism and syscalls, then replays under gdb with reverse execution
candidates.harvest: replayable failure traces and reverse debugging
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: reproduce a captured intermittent failure without rebuilding external state
candidates.requiredDependencies: rr, gdb, supported Linux CPU/kernel/perf configuration
candidates.compatibilityRisks: host CPU/kernel/perf restrictions and record overhead
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: upstream documents deterministic replay for multi-process applications including browsers
candidates.smallestExperiment: record a controlled intermittent Ferrum child failure and replay it
candidates.acceptanceTest: same failure replays with raw Ferrum evidence retained and bounded overhead

candidates.architecture: namespaces, rlimits, cgroups, seccomp/Kafel, mounts and one-shot/re-run modes
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: reduce fixture blast radius with functional/evidence parity
candidates.upstreamIssues: generated policy must be validated and never fail open
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: mature namespace/seccomp sandbox for untrusted workloads
candidates.smallestExperiment: same Ferrum process fixture normal vs no-network/read-only/resource-limited nsjail
candidates.acceptanceTest: identical output/evidence/restart/cleanup plus proven restrictions and bounded setup cost

candidates.architecture: userspace application kernel with runsc, Sentry and Gofer
candidates.requiredDependencies: Linux container runtime plus runsc/KVM or systrap
candidates.upstreamIssues: fit must be measured per workload
candidates.smallestExperiment: same disposable service under default runtime and gVisor after lighter baseline
candidates.acceptanceTest: same task/evidence with quantified overhead and stronger boundary

candidates.architecture: namespace/bind-mount primitive with caller-supplied security policy
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: lower setup overhead if restrictions prove equivalent
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: used by Flatpak and Linux sandboxed apps
candidates.smallestExperiment: repeat qualified nsjail fixture with explicit bubblewrap policy
candidates.acceptanceTest: same restrictions/evidence with lower overhead and no fail-open behavior

candidates.architecture: minimal VMM and jailer around KVM microVMs
candidates.harvest: microVM lifecycle and strong boundary concepts
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: strong isolation for a future workload that genuinely requires it
candidates.compatibilityRisks: provisioning/startup/portability cost disproportionate to current needs
candidates.upstreamIssues: fit is blocker, not upstream quality
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: production microVM runtime for secure multi-tenant workloads
candidates.smallestExperiment: none until VM-grade isolation is required
candidates.acceptanceTest: must beat lighter isolation on a concrete need

candidates.architecture: container runtime backed by lightweight VMs
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: strong boundary while retaining container workflows
candidates.acceptanceTest: unique isolation value with acceptable startup/compatibility

candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: lower fixture startup if container orchestration becomes material
candidates.compatibilityRisks: does not solve a current bottleneck alone
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: active OCI runtime used in container stacks
candidates.smallestExperiment: compare after a stable disposable container fixture exists
candidates.acceptanceTest: material runtime win with identical behavior/cleanup

candidates.architecture: captures process state and restores process trees from images
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: resume expensive deterministic fixture state faster than full setup
candidates.compatibilityRisks: kernel features, privileges, external resources and state portability
candidates.upstreamIssues: capability must be probed per workload
candidates.smallestExperiment: checkpoint/restore one deterministic service fixture and verify identity/behavior
candidates.acceptanceTest: correct identity/task behavior with material time-to-ready win

candidates.harvest: bounded syscall tail only after unexplained process failure
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: faster attribution for pre-log file/network/process failures
candidates.smallestExperiment: controlled missing-file/connect failure with and without bounded capture
candidates.acceptanceTest: new root-cause signal with bounded evidence/overhead and unchanged success path

candidates.architecture: BPF programs on kernel/user probes via high-level tracing language
candidates.harvest: selective probes when syscall traces are insufficient
candidates.smallestExperiment: only after strace cannot explain a controlled issue
candidates.acceptanceTest: unique actionable signal at bounded overhead/evidence volume

candidates.harvest: correlation IDs and processor/export boundary concepts
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: correlate browser/process/service timing in fewer interpretation steps
candidates.requiredDependencies: none for native IDs; Collector only for export experiment
candidates.upstreamIssues: value must exceed native evidence complexity
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: mature modular telemetry pipeline with active releases
candidates.smallestExperiment: correlate one browser+process run to a local Collector while retaining raw evidence
candidates.acceptanceTest: new actionable correlation at bounded bytes/time with native evidence authoritative
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: after native correlation identity is defined

candidates.architecture: trace producers plus Trace Processor/PerfettoSQL over multiple formats
candidates.harvest: optional raw trace sidecar plus SQL-derived timing diagnostics
candidates.expectedMeasurableBenefit: fewer agent calls and faster attribution of long tasks/navigation/process/network timing
candidates.requiredDependencies: Perfetto capture/Trace Processor only when opted in
candidates.platformCoverage: strongest on Android/Linux/Chromium; query processing broader
candidates.compatibilityRisks: trace size, capture overhead and evolving schemas
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Android and Chromium tracing ecosystem with SQL Trace Processor
candidates.smallestExperiment: capture/query one existing browser or Android workload and correlate Ferrum step timestamps
candidates.acceptanceTest: better timing attribution or fewer agent calls with bounded overhead and full raw evidence retained

maximumImprovementChallenge.reason: nsjail, rr, Perfetto, OpenTelemetry, strace and heavier isolation runtimes require identical-workload experiments; immediate integration would be unproven churn.
rejectedShortcuts: Do not make Firecracker, Kata or gVisor core without a workload requiring their stronger boundary.
Do not replace or hide raw Ferrum evidence with telemetry/traces.
Do not let Linux-only tooling reduce Windows/browser/mobile coverage.

nextExperiments: Same deterministic process fixture unisolated vs nsjail with proven network/filesystem/resource restrictions, functional/evidence parity and setup overhead.
Record/replay a controlled intermittent Linux process failure with rr and measure overhead.
Prototype a release-pinned Perfetto sidecar for one browser or Android workload and measure capture/query overhead plus agent-call reduction.
Run a bounded failure-only strace experiment before considering bpftrace.
Evaluate CRIU/gVisor only after lighter replay/isolation paths show an unmet need.
Evaluate OpenTelemetry export only after Ferrum-native correlation identifiers prove useful.
nextResearchCursor: CRIU and stronger isolation only after lighter baselines
telemetry export/correlation after native identity envelope
guardrails: Linux-only sandbox/replay/diagnostic tools remain optional and additive.
Raw hash-verified Ferrum evidence remains authoritative; traces/telemetry/summaries are derived sidecars.
Isolation must prove restrictions and may never fail open.
No viewport/item caps, stale caches, skipped evidence, synthetic-only substitution or weakened validation.
